title: How the Cerebellum Learns from Error

scenes.tts: Damage the cerebellum and a person is not paralysed. They move, and they move badly. Reaches overshoot. The hand shakes as it nears the cup. The cerebellum makes movements accurate, and it learns to keep them accurate. How does it learn?
scenes.caption: Damage the cerebellum and a person is not paralysed. They move, and they move badly. Reaches overshoot. The hand shakes as it nears the cup. The cerebellum makes movements accurate, and it learns to keep them accurate. How does it learn?
scenes.visual: A schematic reach: a hand path leaves a start dot, overshoots the target ring, then wobbles more as it settles; labels name the overshoot and the shaking; a question closes the scene.
scenes.narration: Damage the cerebellum and a person is not paralysed. They move, and they move badly. Reaches overshoot. The hand shakes as it nears the cup. The cerebellum makes movements accurate, and it learns to keep them accurate. How does it learn?

scenes.tts: Here is the circuit. Mossy fibres excite granule cells. Each granule cell sends an axon up to run along the fold as a parallel fibre. Parallel fibres pass through the dendrites of many Purkinje cells. Purkinje cells are the only output of the cerebellar cortex. They release GABA, so they inhibit the deep cerebellar nuclei.

scenes.visual: The circuit is built from labelled boxes and simple neurons: mossy fibre box, granule cells whose axons turn into parallel fibres, a Purkinje cell and a faint neighbour, then an inhibitory arrow to the deep nuclei box.

scenes.tts: The second input is the climbing fibre, from the inferior olive. Each adult Purkinje cell receives one. Simple spikes are ordinary action potentials. A complex spike is a large spike, one for each climbing fibre event. In a made up recording, one hundred thirty simple spikes in two seconds is sixty five hertz. Two complex spikes is one hertz.

scenes.visual: The climbing fibre and inferior olive are added to the circuit; the circuit gives way to a made-up two-second recording with 130 simple-spike ticks and two tall complex-spike ticks, and the two rates are worked beneath.

scenes.tts: Marr and Albus proposed that the climbing fibre is a teacher. When it fires together with some parallel fibres, those synapses change. Ito and Kano paired the two inputs in rabbits. Transmission from parallel fibre to Purkinje cell was depressed for a long time. This is long term depression, or L T D. A weaker synapse means the Purkinje cell fires less in that context. It inhibits its nuclear target less, so the nuclear output rises.

scenes.visual: The climbing fibre and two parallel fibres fire together; their synapse dots shrink and turn red; the Purkinje cell dims, its inhibitory arrow thins, and the deep nuclei box brightens.

scenes.tts: Try it with prism goggles. A made up thrower's first throw lands twenty centimetres to the right. Each throw corrects a fixed fraction, zero point three, of the remaining error. The error falls to fourteen, then nine point eight, then six point eight six. After seven corrections, it is one point six five. Now remove the prisms. The first throw lands about eighteen point four centimetres to the left. The motor command itself was recalibrated.
scenes.caption: Try it with prism goggles. A made-up thrower's first throw lands 20 cm to the right. Each throw corrects a fixed fraction, 0.30, of the remaining error. The error falls to 14.0, then 9.8, then 6.86. After 7 corrections, it is 1.65. Now remove the prisms. The first throw lands about 18.4 cm to the left. The motor command itself was recalibrated.
scenes.visual: Bars of landing error, computed as 20 times 0.7 to the n, shrink with each correction; with the prisms removed one bar drops to the left side, about 18.4 cm.

scenes.tts: The teacher idea has limits. In two monkeys, a complex spike predicted the next trial's output change during gain increase learning of an eye reflex, but not during gain decrease learning. Three mouse lines with no L T D in standard slice tests learned all three tasks normally, though modified protocols induced L T D in slices from two of them. So the teacher's effect is gated, and Marr Albus Ito remains a model. Keep this rule. In the model, the climbing fibre teaches by weakening synapses.

So the teacher's effect is gated, and Marr-Albus-Ito remains a model. Keep this rule. In the model, the climbing fibre teaches by weakening synapses.
scenes.visual: Two evidence cards (two monkeys, gain-increase learning yes, gain-decrease learning no; three mouse lines, three tasks learned) sit above the model chain climbing fibre, weakened synapse, Purkinje cell.
